sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. randomized experiment with fixed finite stratum set \(\mathcal J\), fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A\), and known action probabilities \(e_{ja}\).
sampling_model.units: For each local row \(n\), the full units \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_n\), while the planner observes only \(O^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ni}=(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni})\) and hence only \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditional randomization satisfies \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp A\mid X\), consistency, and \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every stratum has \(p_j\ge p_{\min}\), every randomized action has \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\), and every benchmark action has \(b_{ja}\ge\beta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite randomized cells are estimated by within-cell Hájek means and stratum masses by empirical frequencies. These observed estimators generate \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\), the only frontier supplied to the temperature selector. The Gaussian approximation envelope for the distinct oracle regret path is derived from bounded outcomes, cell mass, and overlap in \(\mathrm{lem:cell\mbox{-}gaussian}\), rather than assumed for the estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed positive \(\lambda\), \(nR_\lambda(\widehat\theta)\) converges to one-half of a Gaussian quadratic form.
A predetermined diverging inverse temperature yields root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for the unsmoothed optimal-policy value.
Convergent binary treatment rules are represented by rules in a shifted Gaussian limit experiment.
A scalar empirical-process supremum is coupled nonasymptotically to the corresponding Gaussian supremum.
The concentration function of a standardized Gaussian-process supremum is bounded by its expected supremum.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian limit is equivalent to full differentiability of the transformation.
Gaussian-vector maxima admit covariance comparison and anti-concentration bounds under arbitrary correlation.
A separation-of-variables transformation reduces Gaussian rectangle probabilities to bounded multiple integration.
Taylor expansion, interval analysis, and automatic differentiation self-validate Gaussian rectangle probabilities.
Recursive integration evaluates noncentered Gaussian orthant probabilities for positive-definite correlation matrices.
Joint Gaussian critical values give coverage after selecting a series dimension from the searched specification set.

body.tldr: A finite-stratum randomized lottery generates a continuum of benchmark-centered Gibbs rules indexed by a KL penalty. The normalized oracle-minus-estimated regret is compactified into one continuous path whose hard endpoint uses benchmark weights on every maximizing set and whose high-penalty endpoint is a projected categorical-covariance quadratic form. The main result is a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation for this entire nonlinear path. An observed plug-in welfare frontier supplies the operational temperature selector, while a deterministic simultaneous-event bridge transfers coverage to the oracle regret at that selected temperature. An effective interval-and-Gaussian-integration algorithm emits a machine-checkable one-sided certificate within an explicit work bound and has a finite analytic fallback. The resulting envelope remains valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice and at quantile atoms. A cellwise atom formula and a legal two-stratum binary collision witness show that the frozen assumptions do not imply a uniform atom-removed small-interval modulus, so two-sided critical-value accuracy requires additional structure even though one-sided honesty does not.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while the hard assignment boundary and softmax inference for one predetermined smoothing sequence are studied separately. No published result gives a quantitative joint law or a certified one-sided critical value over the full penalty menu, and Gaussian-supremum anti-concentration does not cover collisions of the hard-cell atoms exhibited here.
project_justification.niche: Finite multiaction lotteries create a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic: its interior coordinates are nonlinear Gaussian transforms, its hard endpoint is directionally differentiable with benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and its opposite endpoint has a different quadratic normalization. Its hard cells also generate explicitly characterizable atoms whose levels can collide as the local state varies.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the primitive finite-cell Gaussian certificate, matches both endpoints, proves an explicit tie-slab coupling rate in \(C([0,1])\), defines a sample-computable plug-in frontier and its observed-data sigma-field, and turns a verified lower CDF bracket with directed rounding and a finite fallback into computably honest inference after frontier-based temperature choice. It also proves the exact hard-cell atom formula and a fixed legal counterexample to uniform atom-removed anti-concentration, sharply separating the settled one-sided guarantee from unavailable two-sided value accuracy.

body.related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie studies benchmark-centered KL assignment and proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty; its Conclusion leaves data-driven penalty choice open, and its deterministic binary analysis is separate. Its three-arm commitment-savings frontier motivates an illustration, but no finite-stratification adequacy claim is made. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis uses softmax smoothing for one unsmoothed optimal-policy value along a predetermined diverging temperature, a different scalar target. Hirano--Porter supplies the shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment for binary hard treatment choice, not a multiaction path law. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato and Giessing give anti-concentration for Gaussian-process suprema, whereas \(G(h,Z_V)\) is nonlinear and the proved hard-cell atom collisions rule out the requested uniform atom-removed modulus under the present class. Fang--Santos explains directional irregularity but does not furnish atom-safe continuum calibration. Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki provide Gaussian integration components, not certification of this nonlinear continuum event. Kang supplies simultaneous-band selection logic for an observed series path; the present bridge additionally separates the observed selector frontier from the unobserved oracle causal-regret target.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The one-sided algorithm terminates and certifies coverage because work-capped refinement has an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback. It need not return a critical value within a prescribed numerical distance of \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\). The proved two-stratum binary witness shows that no uniform atom-removed modulus follows from the frozen assumptions: distinct positive hard-cell atoms can collide while retaining positive mass. Thus a two-sided value-width certificate would need additional atom separation, a restricted local-state set, or another explicit structural condition. The rational fallback \(2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\) can be conservative.
body.honest_scope: The theorem is uniform only for fixed \(J\) and \(K\), positive benchmark probabilities, positive stratum and treatment probabilities, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, and a covariance spectrum bounded away from zero. It excludes boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing action or stratum counts, disappearing cells, and continuous covariates without a prespecified finite stratification. The commitment-savings display is an illustration conditional on prespecified cells. Temperature selection is restricted to \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable rules, including rules based on the displayed plug-in frontier; that frontier is not claimed to estimate the unobserved oracle regret path. The simultaneous upper envelope and its exact transfer to operational selectors are settled. The requested uniform atom-removed anti-concentration statement is false in general on the declared model, and no two-sided least-favorable quantile-accuracy guarantee is claimed without added separation structure.
body.interpretation: The robust output is deliberately one-sided: it certifies that the entire normalized oracle-regret path lies below one auditable critical value, so any temperature chosen from observed data inherits the same guarantee. The negative concentration theorem is not a failure of coverage. It says that nearby local states can place positive hard-cell atoms arbitrarily close together, preventing a uniform conversion from probability error to critical-value error without further separation or atom-structure assumptions.
